questions.solution:
Take $x$ horizontal and $y$ vertical, $a_x = 0$, $a_y = -g$. Initial components: $u_x = u\cos\theta$, $u_y = u\sin\theta$.
(a) Time of flight: vertical displacement is zero at landing, $y = u_y t - \tfrac{1}{2}gt^2 = 0$, so $t(T) = 2u\sin\theta/g$.
(b) Range: $R = u_x T = u\cos\theta \cdot 2u\sin\theta/g = u^2\sin 2\theta/g$.
(c) For fixed $u$, $R$ is maximum when $\sin 2\theta = 1$, i.e. $2\theta = 90^\circ$, so $\theta = 45^\circ$, giving $R_{\max} = u^2/g$.
questions.question: A projectile is launched from the ground with velocity $u$ at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal. Derive expressions for (a) the time of flight, (b) the horizontal range, and (c) the angle that gives maximum range for a fixed $u$.

questions.solution:
Forces along the plane: component of weight $mg\sin30^\circ$ downwards, friction $f = \mu_k N = \mu_k mg\cos30^\circ$ opposing motion.
Work–energy theorem: $W_{\text{net}} = \Delta K$. $W_{\text{net}} = (mg\sin30^\circ - \mu_k mg\cos30^\circ)\, s$.
Substituting: $mg s(\sin30^\circ - 0.2\cos30^\circ) = 5 \times 10 \times 4 \times (0.5 - 0.2 \times 0.866) = 200 \times (0.5 - 0.173) = 200 \times 0.327 = 65.4\,\mathrm{J}$.
Hence $\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = 65.4$, so $v = \sqrt{2 \times 65.4/5} = \sqrt{26.2} \approx 5.1\,\mathrm{m/s}$.
questions.question: A block of mass $m = 5\,\mathrm{kg}$ slides down a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal with coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu_k = 0.2$. Using the work–energy theorem, find its speed after sliding $s = 4\,\mathrm{m}$ from rest. (Take $g = 10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$.)

questions.solution: On a flat curve friction alone supplies the centripetal force: $f_s = mv^2/r \le \mu_s N = \mu_s mg$. The limiting speed is $v_{\max} = \sqrt{\mu_s g r} = \sqrt{0.4 \times 10 \times 50} = \sqrt{200} \approx 14.1\,\mathrm{m/s}$ (about $51\,\mathrm{km/h}$). Any faster and the required centripetal force exceeds maximum static friction, so the car skids.
questions.question: A car of mass $1000\,\mathrm{kg}$ rounds a flat (unbanked) curve of radius $50\,\mathrm{m}$. If the coefficient of static friction between tyres and road is $0.4$, what is the maximum safe speed? ($g = 10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$)

questions.solution:
Newton's law: every mass attracts every other with $F = GMm/r^2$ along the line joining them.
At height $h$, distance from Earth's centre is $r = R + h$, so $mg_h = GMm/(R+h)^2$, giving $g_h = GM/(R+h)^2$.
At the surface $g = GM/R^2$, hence $g_h/g = R^2/(R+h)^2 = 1/(1 + h/R)^2$, which falls as $h$ grows — gravity weakens with altitude.
At $h = R$: $g_h/g = 1/(1+1)^2 = 1/4$, so gravity is one-quarter of its surface value.
questions.question: State Newton's law of gravitation. Derive the expression for acceleration due to gravity $g$ at a height $h$ above Earth's surface (radius $R$, mass $M$), and show that $g$ decreases with altitude. Evaluate the ratio $g_h/g$ at $h = R$.
